items.headline: Police warn job seekers about paying 'agents' who promise to get them a job
items.summary: A 42-year-old woman is being charged for allegedly taking money from job applicants after promising to help them land jobs in Singapore, then spending it on other things. Police believe she is linked to several similar cases and urge job seekers to question any request for upfront fees, especially ones described as legal, admin or processing charges. If you're job hunting from India, only use agencies you can verify, and contact your bank and file a police report straight away if you think you've been scammed.

items.headline: US tariff plan for Singapore is still only a proposal, analysts say
items.summary: The US has proposed a tariff of up to 20% on Singapore's exports, alongside similar moves against 13 other markets. Analysts point out that it is still open to public consultation, that there is room to negotiate and that some products may be excluded, so they expect limited impact in the near term.

items.headline: More covered walkways and bigger sun and rain shelters on the way
items.summary: Developers can now build roof eaves and sun-shading up to 3m wide, up from 2m, without it counting against how much floor space they're allowed. Covered linkways also no longer need to be part of a landscaped area to qualify. The aim is better protection from heat and heavier rain as the climate changes.

items.headline: HYROX fitness races at Singapore EXPO this weekend, with a first race for kids
items.summary: The first AIA HYROX Youngstars race in Singapore, for children aged 8 to 15, takes place at Singapore EXPO on 28 and 29 November. It mixes running with eight exercise stations, scaled for each age group. Worth a look if you're nearby with fitness-mad kids.
